title: Unborn Babies to Count Toward Priority for Taiwan's Social Housing
summaryZh: 社宅優先順序新制：胎兒也算入子女人數
summaryHi: ताइवान में सामाजिक आवास की प्राथमिकता तय करते समय अब गर्भस्थ शिशु भी बच्चों में गिने जाएँगे।
summaryEs: En Taiwán, los bebés aún no nacidos contarán como hijos para obtener prioridad en la vivienda social.
summaryJa: 台湾の社会住宅の優先入居で、おなかの赤ちゃんも子どもの数に数えられることに。
summaryKo: 타이완 사회주택 우선순위를 정할 때 이제 태아도 자녀 수에 포함된다.
summaryEn: Unborn babies will now count as children when Taiwan decides which families get priority for social housing.
paragraphs: Expectant parents in Taiwan will soon have a better chance of getting social housing. The Ministry of the Interior has announced that unborn babies will count, alongside children under 18, when deciding which families receive priority for government-subsidised rental homes.

The change follows an amendment to Article 4 of the Housing Act earlier this year. Under the revised law, at least 20 percent of social housing units must be set aside for newly married couples, meaning those married for less than two years, and for families raising children under 18. The more children a family has, the higher its priority.

The ministry's implementing regulations, published on 11 November, spell out how children should be counted. To show that a woman is pregnant, applicants can provide her maternal health handbook, which is usually issued between the eighth and twelfth week of pregnancy, or a medical certificate from a healthcare provider. Other documents may also be accepted if officials consider them sufficient.
In its explanatory notes, the ministry said giving priority to expectant families fits with the government's wider push to encourage childbirth.
The Housing Act also requires that at least 40 percent of social housing go to people who are economically or socially disadvantaged.
In Taiwan, some families can rent cheap homes from the government. These homes are called social housing.
Families with more children can get these homes first. Now the rules have changed. A baby that is not born yet will also count as a child.
The Ministry of the Interior made the new rules on 11 November. A pregnant woman can show her mother and baby health book. She can also show a letter from a doctor or a hospital.

Earlier this year, Taiwan changed its housing law. Now at least 20 percent of social homes must be for new couples or families with children under 18. New couples are people married for less than two years.
The government says the change will help families who want to have babies. Taiwan wants more children to be born.

現在規定改了。
還沒出生的寶寶也會算作一個孩子。
內政部在 11 月 11 日訂定了新規定。
懷孕的女性可以出示她的孕婦健康手冊。
她也可以出示醫生或醫院開的證明。
今年稍早，台灣修改了住宅法。
現在至少 20% 的社會住宅必須給新婚夫妻或有未滿 18 歲子女的家庭。
新婚夫妻是指結婚未滿兩年的人。
政府說，這項改變將幫助想生寶寶的家庭。
台灣希望有更多孩子出生。

paragraphs: Taiwan's Ministry of the Interior says unborn babies will now count when the government decides which families get social housing first. Social housing is low-cost rental housing paid for by the government.

Earlier this year, Taiwan changed Article 4 of its Housing Act. The new law says that at least 20 percent of social housing must be kept for couples who have been married for less than two years, or for families with children under 18. Families with more children get higher priority.
The ministry's new rules, published on 11 November, explain how to count children. Both children under 18 and babies who are not yet born are included.

To prove a pregnancy, a family can show the mother's health handbook, which women usually get between the eighth and twelfth week of pregnancy. A medical certificate from a hospital or clinic is also accepted.

The ministry said that helping families who are expecting a baby supports the government's efforts to encourage people to have children. The law also keeps at least 40 percent of social housing for people with financial or social difficulties.

今年稍早，台灣修改了《住宅法》第 4 條。
新法規定，至少 20% 的社會住宅必須保留給結婚未滿兩年的夫妻，或有未滿 18 歲子女的家庭。
子女越多的家庭，優先順序越高。
內政部在 11 月 11 日公布的新規定，說明了子女如何計算。
未滿 18 歲的子女和尚未出生的胎兒都包括在內。
要證明懷孕，家庭可以出示母親的孕婦健康手冊，女性通常在懷孕第八到第十二週拿到。
醫院或診所開立的診斷證明也會被接受。

法律也保留至少 40% 的社會住宅給有經濟或社會困難的人。

paragraphs: Expectant parents in Taiwan will soon have a better chance of getting social housing. The Ministry of the Interior has announced that unborn babies will count, alongside children under 18, when deciding which families receive priority for government-subsidised rental homes.

The change follows an amendment to Article 4 of the Housing Act earlier this year. Under the revised law, at least 20 percent of social housing units must be set aside for newly married couples, meaning those married for less than two years, and for families raising children under 18. The more children a family has, the higher its priority.

The ministry's implementing regulations, published on 11 November, spell out how children should be counted. To show that a woman is pregnant, applicants can provide her maternal health handbook, which is usually issued between the eighth and twelfth week of pregnancy, or a medical certificate from a healthcare provider. Other documents may also be accepted if officials consider them sufficient.
In its explanatory notes, the ministry said giving priority to expectant families fits with the government's wider push to encourage childbirth.
The Housing Act also requires that at least 40 percent of social housing go to people who are economically or socially disadvantaged.
sentZh: 台灣的準父母很快就有更大機會申請到社會住宅。
內政部宣布，在決定哪些家庭可優先租用政府補貼的住宅時，胎兒將與未滿 18 歲的子女一併計算。
這項改變源自今年稍早《住宅法》第 4 條的修正。
根據修正後的法律，至少 20% 的社會住宅單位必須保留給新婚夫妻（即結婚未滿兩年者）以及養育未滿 18 歲子女的家庭。
家庭的子女越多，優先順序就越高。
內政部 11 月 11 日公布的施行規定，清楚說明了子女應如何計算。
要證明女性懷孕，申請人可提供她的孕婦健康手冊（通常在懷孕第八到第十二週發給），或醫療院所開立的診斷證明。
若官員認為足夠，其他文件也可能被接受。
內政部在說明中表示，讓準父母家庭享有優先權，符合政府鼓勵生育的整體政策。
《住宅法》也規定，至少 40% 的社會住宅必須提供給經濟或社會弱勢者。

paragraphs: Families expecting a baby in Taiwan are set to move up the queue for social housing. The Ministry of the Interior has issued new regulations under which unborn children, as well as children under 18, will be taken into account when determining which households qualify for priority access to government-subsidised rental homes.

The move stems from an amendment to Article 4 of the Housing Act passed earlier this year. It obliges authorities to reserve at least 20 percent of social housing units for couples who have been married for under two years and for households with children under 18, with larger families ranked higher.

The implementing rules, published on 11 November, clarify how children are to be counted. Applicants can verify a pregnancy by submitting the maternal health handbook, which is typically issued between the eighth and twelfth week, a medical certificate from a healthcare institution, or other documentation that officials deem adequate.
In explanatory notes accompanying the rules, the ministry argued that prioritising expectant families is consistent with the government's broader drive to raise the birth rate.

Separately, the Housing Act stipulates that no less than 40 percent of units must be allocated to economically or socially disadvantaged groups, so the new rules sit alongside existing protections for vulnerable tenants.
sentZh: 在台灣，正在等待寶寶出生的家庭，申請社會住宅的順位即將往前移。
內政部發布新規定，在判定哪些家戶有資格優先租用政府補貼住宅時，除了未滿 18 歲的子女，胎兒也將納入考量。
此舉源自今年稍早通過的《住宅法》第 4 條修正案。
該條要求主管機關保留至少 20% 的社會住宅單位給結婚未滿兩年的夫妻及有未滿 18 歲子女的家戶，家庭人數越多，排序越前面。
11 月 11 日公布的施行細則，釐清了子女應如何計算。
申請人可提交孕婦健康手冊（通常在第八到第十二週發給）、醫療機構開立的診斷證明，或官員認為適當的其他文件來證明懷孕。
內政部在隨附的說明中主張，讓準父母家庭優先，與政府提高出生率的整體努力一致。
另外，《住宅法》規定至少 40% 的單位必須分配給經濟或社會弱勢族群，因此新規定與現有保障弱勢房客的措施並行。

paragraphs: Taiwan has introduced a notable change to the way social housing is allocated. According to newly issued regulations from the Ministry of the Interior, unborn children will now be counted alongside minors when assessing a household's eligibility for priority access to state-subsidised rental accommodation.

This measure derives from an amendment to Article 4 of the Housing Act enacted earlier this year. The revised legislation mandates that a minimum of 20 percent of social housing units be reserved for couples married for less than two years and for families with children under 18, with priority increasing in proportion to the number of children.

The implementing regulations, which were published on 11 November, specify the criteria for counting children. Pregnancy may be verified through the maternal health handbook, generally issued between the eighth and twelfth week of gestation, a medical certificate from a healthcare institution, or alternative documentation considered sufficient by the authorities.

The ministry justified the policy by stating that granting precedence to expectant families aligns with the government's broader strategy to promote childbirth, an increasingly pressing issue given Taiwan's persistently low birth rate.

Notably, the Act also requires that at least 40 percent of units be allocated to economically or socially disadvantaged applicants, ensuring that the new provision complements rather than replaces existing safeguards.
sentZh: 台灣對社會住宅的分配方式做出一項值得注意的改變。
根據內政部新發布的規定，在評估家戶是否有資格優先租用國家補貼的住宅時，胎兒將與未成年子女一併計算。
這項措施源自今年稍早制定的《住宅法》第 4 條修正。
修正後的法律規定，至少 20% 的社會住宅單位須保留給結婚未滿兩年的夫妻及有未滿 18 歲子女的家庭，且優先順序隨子女人數按比例提高。
11 月 11 日公布的施行細則，明定了子女計算的標準。
懷孕可透過孕婦健康手冊（通常於妊娠第八到第十二週發給）、醫療機構開立的診斷證明，或主管機關認為足夠的其他文件來證明。
內政部為這項政策辯護，表示給予準父母家庭優先權，符合政府促進生育的整體策略；鑑於台灣出生率長期偏低，這個問題日益迫切。
值得注意的是，該法也規定至少 40% 的單位必須分配給經濟或社會弱勢的申請人，確保新條款是對既有保障措施的補充，而非取代。

noteJa.usage: mandate + 名詞 / that 節；名詞 mandate は「委任」。

noteKo.usage: mandate + 명사 / that 절; 명사 mandate는 '위임'.

noteEn.usage: 'mandate that...' or 'mandate training'. Noun: a mandate.

married.ex: They have been married for three years.

maternal.en: relating to mothers, especially giving birth

meaning.ex: The shop is closed, meaning we must go elsewhere.

measure.en: an official action to deal with something
measure.ex: The city took new measures to cut traffic.

medical.en: connected with medicine and treating illness
medical.ex: She needs medical help after the fall.

minimum.ex: The minimum age for the job is 18.

ministry.ex: The ministry released new rules for schools.

ministry's.ex: The ministry's report came out today.

minors.ex: Shops cannot sell alcohol to minors.

mother.en: a woman who has a child

mother's.ex: The mother's handbook records the baby's health.

move.en: an action to achieve something; (v.) to change position
move.ex: The move will save money for families.

newly.ex: The newly built school opens soon.

not.ex: The shop is not open today.

notable.ex: There was a notable rise in sales.

notably.ex: Notably, prices fell in rural areas.

notes.ex: The teacher added notes to explain the hard words.

number.ex: The number of visitors fell this year.

obliges.en: makes someone do something by law or rule
obliges.ex: The rule obliges shops to close early.

officials.en: people who work for a government
officials.ex: Officials say there is no plan.

out.en: away from the shore or inside
out.ex: The boat sailed out to sea.

paid.ex: The trip was paid for by the school.

passed.en: went successfully through (a stage or test)
passed.ex: The bill was passed by parliament in May.

people.ex: Many people came to the event.

percent.ex: Ten percent of the class was absent.

persistently.en: for a long time without stopping

policy.ex: The new housing policy starts in May.

example.en: Safety must take precedence over speed.

note.usage: 固定搭配 take precedence (over sth)。

noteHi.exampleTr: सुरक्षा को गति पर प्राथमिकता मिलनी चाहिए।
noteHi.usage: take precedence (over sth) निश्चित वाक्यांश है।

noteEs.exampleTr: La seguridad debe tener prioridad sobre la velocidad.
noteEs.usage: Frase fija: take precedence over algo.

noteJa.exampleTr: 安全は速さより優先されなければならない。
noteJa.usage: take precedence (over ～) の決まった形。

noteEn.meaning: the right to be dealt with first.

pregnancy.en: the time when a woman has a baby growing inside her
pregnancy.ex: She felt tired in early pregnancy.

pressing.en: needing to be dealt with now
pressing.ex: Cost of living is the most pressing problem.

prioritising.ex: The school is prioritising reading this year.

priority.zh: 優先事項（top priority：首要任務）

promote.en: to help something grow or happen
promote.ex: The town wants to promote cycling.

proportion.ex: A large proportion of staff work from home.

prove.ex: The plan may prove too costly.

provider.en: a person or organisation that supplies a service
provider.ex: Ask your healthcare provider for advice.

provision.en: a part of a law that says what must happen
provision.ex: The new provision protects older workers.

push.en: to force or move someone towards something
push.ex: High rents push young people out of cities.

qualify.en: to have the right to get

queue.en: a line of people waiting their turn
queue.ex: There was a long online queue for the tickets.

raise.ex: The shop will raise its prices next month.

raising.en: looking after children until they grow up
raising.ex: She is raising two children on her own.

ranked.en: put in a position on a list
ranked.ex: The city was ranked first for safety.

rate.en: level or amount, often a percentage
rate.ex: The success rate of the treatment is high.

rather.ex: Walk rather than drive if you can.

receive.ex: You will receive a letter next week.

regulations.ex: New regulations will limit noise near schools.

rent.en: money paid to live in a home
rent.ex: The rent is due on Monday.

replaces.ex: The new model replaces the old one.

reserve.en: to keep something for a special person or use
reserve.ex: The restaurant will reserve a table for us.

reserved.en: kept for a particular person or group
reserved.ex: These seats are reserved for older passengers.

revised.ex: The revised timetable starts next week.

safeguards.ex: The law has strong safeguards for workers.

note.usage: 常見 legal safeguards、put safeguards in place、safeguards against。

example.en: The law includes safeguards to protect older workers.
example.zh: 該法包含保護年長勞工的保障措施。

noteHi.usage: legal safeguards, safeguards against आम हैं।
noteHi.exampleTr: क़ानून में बुज़ुर्ग कर्मचारियों की सुरक्षा के उपाय हैं।

noteEs.exampleTr: La ley incluye garantías para proteger a los trabajadores mayores.

noteJa.usage: legal safeguards、safeguards against などが多い。
noteJa.exampleTr: その法律には高齢労働者を守る保護措置がある。

noteKo.exampleTr: 그 법에는 고령 노동자를 보호하는 장치가 있다.

noteEn.meaning: rules or measures that protect people from harm.

says.ex: The report says costs will rise.

separately.ex: Each case will be judged separately.

set.ex: We hit the goal set by the manager.

should.en: used to give advice or say what is likely

show.ex: The figures show a big rise.

sit.en: to exist or be placed in a position
sit.ex: The new rules sit alongside the old ones.

so.en: to such a degree; even so = despite that
so.ex: It was so cold that we stayed home.
so.zh: 如此；（even so：儘管如此；so many：這麼多）

social.ex: Social services help families in need.

socially.en: in a way connected with society
socially.ex: The scheme helps socially isolated people.

soon.ex: Soon after, it began to rain.

specify.ex: Please specify the date of your arrival.

spell.en: spell out: explain clearly in detail
spell.ex: The rules spell out what firms must tell customers.

state-subsidised.en: partly paid for by the state
state-subsidised.ex: Many students live in state-subsidised housing.

stating.ex: She left, stating she was tired.

stipulates.ex: The contract stipulates a fixed price.

example.en: The law stipulates that drivers must carry a licence.
example.zh: 法律規定駕駛人必須攜帶駕照。

note.usage: 常用 stipulate that + 子句（子句常用原形動詞或 must）。

noteHi.exampleTr: कानून तय करता है कि ड्राइवर लाइसेंस साथ रखें।
noteHi.meaning: नियम के रूप में तय करना।

noteEs.exampleTr: La ley estipula que los conductores deben llevar el carné.

noteJa.exampleTr: 法律は運転者が免許を携帯するよう定めている。
noteJa.usage: stipulate that + 節 の形が多い。

noteKo.exampleTr: 법은 운전자가 면허증을 소지해야 한다고 규정한다.

noteEn.meaning: to state something as a firm rule.

strategy.en: a plan to reach a goal
strategy.ex: The company needs a new strategy.

submitting.ex: He is submitting his report today.

sufficient.ex: There are sufficient funds for now.

supports.ex: The plan supports small local shops.

taiwan.en: an island country in East Asia

taken.hi: (taken into account: ध्यान में रखा गया)
taken.ex: All views will be taken into account.

tenants.en: people who rent from a landlord

this.en: the thing here or just said

typically.ex: Trains are typically late in winter.

unborn.ex: Smoking can harm an unborn baby.

units.en: separate homes in a building or scheme
units.ex: The project will build 300 new housing units.

up.en: towards a higher or more forward position
up.ex: Prices went up again this month.

usually.ex: I usually have tea for breakfast.

verified.en: shown or checked to be true
verified.ex: Your age must be verified with an ID card.

verify.en: to check that something is true

example.en: Please bring a passport to verify your identity.
example.zh: 請攜帶護照以核實身分。

note.usage: 受詞多為 identity、information、claims；名詞 verification。IELTS 寫作常用來替代 check。

noteHi.exampleTr: पहचान सत्यापित करने के लिए पासपोर्ट लाएँ।
noteHi.usage: identity, information के साथ; संज्ञा verification।

noteEs.exampleTr: Traiga su pasaporte para verificar su identidad.
noteEs.usage: Con identity, information, claims; sustantivo verification.

noteJa.exampleTr: 本人確認のためパスポートをお持ちください。
noteJa.usage: identity, information などを目的語に。名詞 verification。

noteKo.usage: identity, information 등이 목적어; 명사 verification.

noteEn.meaning: to check that something is true or correct.

vulnerable.en: easily hurt or needing special care
vulnerable.ex: The plan helps vulnerable older people.

want.en: to wish to have or do

way.en: a method; how something is done (pay its way：自給自足)
way.ex: There is no other way to do it.

week.ex: I go swimming twice a week.

well.ex: Wages are still well below the national average.
well.ja: かなり（well below：大きく下回る）

were.ex: The roads were busy this morning.

which.en: used to add information about a thing

who.en: used to add information about a person

wider.ex: The benefits should reach the wider city.

women.ex: More women now work in science.
